feedback.problem:
Find where the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{x}+\frac{6}{\sqrt{x}}$ at the point  $(4,5)$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The tangent intersects the $y$-axis at
$($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}} $).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x}+\frac{6}{\sqrt{x}}.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}+\frac{6}{\sqrt{x}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})+6\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{1/2})+6\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}+6\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}){x}^{-3/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={f}^{′}(4) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{{4}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-\frac{3}{8} \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-5 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-4) \\ y & =-\frac{1}{8}x+\frac{1}{2}+5 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{8}x+\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{1}{8}(0)+\frac{11}{2} \\ y & =\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(0,\frac{11}{2}).$
